title: Reading Controlled SOPs and Work Orders

content.overview: Technician I workers must identify the current controlled instruction, reconcile it with the specific work order and physical situation, understand prerequisites and acceptance criteria, and stop when the instruction set is incomplete, contradictory or outside scope.

vocabulary.definition: A controlled standard operating procedure describing how an activity is performed within its defined scope.
An instruction assigning a specific task, location, material, timing, quantity or asset under a controlled procedure.
A document or electronic view whose identity, revision/effective status and distribution are managed by the organization's document-control process.
Defined conditions that indicate whether a step, result or completed task meets requirements.

sections.title: The instruction and assignment answer different questions
sections.body: The SOP defines the controlled method and scope; the work order identifies the specific room, material, batch, asset, quantity, timing or other assignment. Competent execution requires both to agree with physical reality before work proceeds.

sections.title: Current status matters more than familiarity
sections.body: A printed page, screenshot, local file or remembered routine can be obsolete even when it looks official. The technician uses the facility's document-control method to establish the current approved instruction rather than relying on habit or the copy that is easiest to access.

sections.title: Conflicts stay open until resolved
sections.body: A technician does not blend two revisions, silently correct identifiers, or choose whichever instruction is more convenient. A conflict between the SOP, work order, physical label, asset, room or actual condition remains an open issue until the authorized process resolves it.

workedExamples: An older printed SOP is found beside a current controlled digital revision; the technician follows document-control procedure before working.
A room assignment conflicts with the listed batch identifier, so movement pauses until the mismatch is resolved.
The work order quantity is 48 plants but only 47 matching identifiers are present; the technician does not invent the missing identity or silently change the count.
The SOP requires a completion measurement before release, so the task remains open even though the physical work appears finished.
commonMistakes: Following an obsolete procedure because it is familiar or physically located in the room.
Combining steps from two revisions to create an unofficial hybrid procedure.
Silently changing a room, batch, quantity or asset identifier to make the work order match reality.
Ignoring acceptance criteria or required records once the physical task looks complete.
Starting first and planning to clarify a known instruction conflict later.
content.practicalApplication: Audit a mock SOP, work order and physical identification packet. Establish the current instruction, verify scope/prerequisites, reconcile identifiers and quantities, identify acceptance criteria and records, and write a stop/escalation note for every unresolved conflict.
content.summary: Controlled work begins with a defensible instruction set. Technicians establish the current procedure, reconcile the specific assignment to physical reality, understand what proves completion, and leave conflicts open until the authorized process resolves them.

blocks.title: Read the instruction as a controlled object
blocks.body: Before acting, verify which instruction governs the task and whether it is the current controlled version. A familiar printed page, remembered routine, screenshot or locally saved copy can be obsolete even when it looks official. The technician uses the facility's document-control process rather than choosing the version that is easiest to reach.

blocks.alt: Annotated controlled SOP showing document identity and revision, scope and prerequisites, material or asset identity, step sequence, acceptance criteria, required records, and escalation points, beside a work-order card containing the specific room, batch, asset, quantity, date, and shift context.
blocks.caption: The SOP defines the controlled method; the work order applies that method to specific work. A conflict must be resolved, not guessed away.

blocks.title: Seven checks before controlled work begins

items.title: Establish the controlling instruction
items.body: Confirm the instruction ID, revision/effective status and the facility's indication that the version is current.

items.title: Confirm scope
items.body: Verify that this procedure actually covers the task, equipment, area and material involved.

items.title: Verify prerequisites
items.body: Confirm required training, authorization, PPE, tools, setup, permits or prerequisite conditions are present.

items.title: Reconcile assignment identifiers
items.body: Match room, batch/material, asset, quantity, date/shift and other work-order details to the physical labels or system records.

items.title: Find acceptance criteria
items.body: Know what observable condition, measurement, check or approval demonstrates successful completion.

items.title: Find required records
items.body: Know which identities, observations, measurements, times, exceptions or signoffs must be captured as work occurs.

items.title: Locate decision and escalation points
items.body: Know which conditions require clarification, hold, stop-work, approval or transfer before you reach them in the workflow.

blocks.title: Instruction conflicts and the correct Technician I response
rows: Printed revision differs from controlled system
Establish the current approved version through document control before affected work
Work-order room and physical batch label disagree
Stop the affected movement and resolve identity through the authorized process
Start the task and obtain it later
Do not start the affected work until the prerequisite or authorized exception is resolved
Mark complete because the physical step is finished
Keep the task open and escalate/resolve the missing verification
Procedure does not cover the actual condition
Preserve the condition and obtain authorized direction rather than extending scope yourself

blocks.title: The binder copy and controlled digital copy disagree
blocks.setting: A printed SOP in the grow room says Revision 4. The controlled document system shows Revision 6 as effective. Revision 6 changed one verification step. A coworker says the binder copy is what everyone uses.
blocks.prompt: What is the strongest Technician I response?
options: Use Revision 4 because it is physically located in the room
Use whichever version has the faster workflow
Follow the facility's document-control process and use the confirmed current instruction before affected work
Combine the steps from both versions
blocks.answer: Follow the facility's document-control process and use the confirmed current instruction before affected work.
blocks.feedback: Familiarity and physical location do not establish document status. A controlled process should identify the current authorized version and address obsolete copies.

blocks.title: The work order and physical identifiers disagree
blocks.setting: A work order directs movement of Batch B17 from Room 3. The physical tray label says Batch B71, while the destination and quantity otherwise match the order.
options: Assume the tray label has a typo and move it
Change the tray label to B17
Pause the affected movement, preserve both identifiers and resolve the conflict through the authorized process
Move it and add a note after the shift
blocks.answer: Pause the affected movement, preserve both identifiers and resolve the conflict through the authorized process.
blocks.feedback: A near-match is still an identity conflict. Silent correction or assumption can damage traceability and make later reconstruction impossible.

blocks.title: Controlled-instruction pre-task readback
blocks.description: A short pre-task readback makes the instruction and assignment testable instead of relying on memory.

fields.label: Instruction ID / revision
fields.value: Current controlled identifier and effective version/status

fields.label: Scope
fields.value: Task, area, asset and material the instruction covers

fields.label: Prerequisites
fields.value: Training, PPE, setup, tools, authorization or conditions needed before starting

fields.label: Work-order identifiers
fields.value: Room, batch/material, asset, quantity, date/shift or other assigned context

fields.label: Required records
fields.value: Measurements, identities, times, observations, exceptions or signoffs that must be captured

fields.label: Stop / escalation points
fields.value: Conditions requiring clarification, approval, hold, stop-work or referral

fields.label: Open conflicts
fields.value: Anything that does not reconcile and must be resolved before affected work

blocks.note: A mismatch between instruction, assignment and physical reality remains open until an authorized process resolves it.

blocks.title: Audit a controlled work packet
blocks.instructions: Review a supplied SOP, work order, room map and physical-label packet containing an obsolete revision cue, identity mismatch, missing prerequisite and overlooked acceptance criterion.
prompts: Identify the evidence that establishes the current instruction.
Confirm whether the task is within scope.
List every prerequisite and mark whether it is satisfied.
Reconcile each work-order identifier to the physical packet.
Find every conflict and explain why it cannot be silently corrected.
Identify the acceptance criterion and required records that prove completion.
Write the minimum useful escalation note for each unresolved issue.

blocks.title: Remediation cue
blocks.body: If you are choosing which conflicting instruction 'makes more sense,' blending revisions, or correcting identifiers yourself, stop. The technician's role is to detect and preserve the conflict, not erase it.

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.body: MHRA GxP data-integrity guidance is used here as a transferable model for controlled records and reconstructability. It is not presented as a claim that UK pharmaceutical GxP rules govern U.S. cannabis cultivation.

blocks.title: Key takeaway
blocks.body: Controlled work starts before the physical task. Establish the current instruction, reconcile the specific assignment to physical reality, understand what success looks like, and surface conflicts while there is still time to resolve them correctly.
